metadata.title: Cyclic self-sumset recognition: a credited corollary of the integer hardness theorem
metadata.description: Credited exposition of the cyclic consequence of the integer hardness theorem of Abboud, Fischer, Safier, and Wallheimer. Ordinary all-pair self-sumset recognition in the same Z/nZ, with unbounded positive input n, is NP-complete separately for binary n with an explicit binary residue list and for an n-bit characteristic vector. Hardness holds already for odd n and nonempty B containing 0 with every canonical 2b<n. The universal proof gives integer normalization and an odd zero-anchor/no-wrap transfer; dense hardness uses the AFWS uniform 3SAT numerical bound 2^57(v+c)^4. A deterministic polynomial-time exact decision algorithm in either model exists iff P=NP. No new hardness gadget, novelty, first-publication, independent-discovery, or worldwide-openness claim is made. Extensive AI assistance was used in reasoning, source work, adversarial checking, coding, computational verification and writing. Unrefereed; no external human peer review or formal certification. Support includes byte-preserved original records and authored verification code, not third-party source bodies. Inspected AFWS proof: arXiv2410.18661v2 (26 October 2024); SODA2025 publication metadata separately verified.
metadata.notes: Alec Kriebel is the sole named author. OpenAI Codex AI systems were used extensively. Exact historical priority of the cyclic formulation is unknown. Prepared locally on 2026-10-14 before deposit or publication.
